CausalChain: Chronic liver insult (HBV/HCV infection or NAFLD) -> Dysregulation of m6A regulators (upregulation of METTL3 and altered FTO activity) -> Aberrant m6A modification on lncRNAs -> Altered lncRNA stability and processing -> Modulation of cytokine and immune checkpoint (e.g., PD-L1) expression -> Creation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment -> Enhanced tumor immune evasion
Hypothesis: Aberrant m6A modification of lncRNAs in HCC reprograms the tumor immune microenvironment by dysregulating cytokine and immune checkpoint expression, thereby promoting immune evasion and contributing to resistance to immunotherapy. Targeting this m6A-lncRNA axis may enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in liver cancer.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by complex epigenetic and post‐transcriptional dysregulation, among which aberrant m6A RNA modifications play a pivotal role. Emerging evidence links m6A machinery to tumor cell proliferation, metastasis, and immune modulation. In this context, we propose that deregulated m6A modification of selective long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) reprograms the tumor immune microenvironment in HCC. Specifically, overexpression of m6A writer proteins such as METTL3 and/or imbalanced activity of erasers like FTO in HCC leads to altered m6A methylation on lncRNAs. This epitranscriptomic modification influences the stability and processing of these lncRNAs, which in turn modulate the expression of key immune regulators including cytokines and immune checkpoint molecules such as PD-L1. The resultant immunosuppressive milieu facilitates tumor immune evasion and may underlie resistance to immune checkpoint therapies. Thus, targeting the m6A-lncRNA regulatory axis could pave the way for novel therapeutic interventions aimed at enhancing anti-tumor immunity in liver cancer.
